summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Sunrise Health through an Optimize-focused lab comparing INT8 and FP8 quant profiles using their clinical triage prompts. Discussion covered latency vs fidelity tradeoffs, fallback rules, and private deployment constraints. Customer requested sandbox access, security docs, and a short POC to validate quality at target latency.
topics: Private deployment / KMS and audit logs
Benchmarking plan and POC next steps
transcript:
Header: 2027-09-14 08:30 PT | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Maya, Raj, Lina - Redwood; Elaine, Marco, Priya, Jonas - Sunrise

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from Redwood, im gonna hand over to raj for the nitty gritty but we'll try to keep this interactive, ok?
[00:22] Raj: morning all - quick agenda: run the optimize lab, show int eight vs f p eight profiles, heatmap, then Qs and next steps. apologies for any audio noise, my mic's a little hot.
[00:39] Marco: sounds good, we'd love to see realistic latency on our triage prompts and any fidelity regressions.
[00:51] Priya: timeline wise, we want to land something small in pilot by late october, need SLAs for 200ms p50 if possible.
[01:07] Raj: got it, we'll show typical p50 numbers; note that p50 target depends a lot on sequence lengths and batching, and on whether you use dedicated or hosted.
[01:25] Elaine: quick qual - we usually run 3k token prompts for context, mostly clinical notes plus structured fields. want to be careful about hallucinations.
[01:40] Raj: perfect, we'll use your sample prompts later in the sandbox. ok demo start - opening Optimize console — bear with me, the UI recorded name shows 'Redwood Optimise' in some older exports, ignore that.
[02:05] Raj: first slide is the precision heatmap, this maps quality delta vs latency delta between profiles. on the left: baseline fp16, middle: int8, right: fp8 variants. i know sometimes the labels show 'in t eight' or 'f-p eight' in auto captions, ignore that artifact.
[02:33] Raj: here's a live example - using their shorter triage prompt (avg 350 tokens), baseline fp16 p50 240ms, int8 p50 160ms, fp8 p50 140ms. quality measured by our rerank eval and a blind human check.
[02:51] Elaine: how big is the quality delta, practically? any failures in triage label accuracy?
[03:05] Raj: good question — the rerank score drops ~1.8% for int8 on this workload, fp8 is ~0.6% drop. for clinical critical labels we saw a few edge cases where int8 changed the suggested disposition, so we flag those in the fidelity lane.
[03:30] Priya: can we do mixed precision - route sensitive prompts to fp8 and bulk to int8?
[03:42] Raj: yes that's the common pattern — Redwood Optimize supports route-based precision profiles, and you can set rules on prompt size, tags, or confidence thresholds. the console shows a canary rollout slider.
[04:05] Maya: important to call out that the runtime supports automatic fallback - e.g., if int8 returns low-confidence, request can be retried against fp8 variant; we call that the fidelity fallback.
[04:26] Jonas: are there any extra infra costs for fp8? GPUs cost diff?
[04:35] Raj: fp8 can be slightly more compute-bound on older kernels, but our optimizer picks kernels and packing to minimize overhead. typically fp8 cost is within ~5-10% of int8 on our VM mix, but compared to fp16 it's lower.
[04:56] Marco: what about KV cache — does quantization impact long-context performance?
[05:07] Raj: quant affects weight representation, KV cache behavior is orthogonal but some quantized kernels need different packing that can change cache hits slightly — we've seen small variance but nothing dramatic. sometimes captions say 'K-V cash' in transcripts, ha.
[05:27] Elaine: security question — if we go private (VPC on prem) how's KMS handled? do you allow HSM or customer-managed keys?
[05:38] Maya: yes, private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations; we'll send the SOC2 and KMS integration doc. there's an audit log that records token-level tracing but you can toggle retention.
[05:55] Raj: jumping back to the lab — opening the heatmap overlay, you can click each cell to see a sample degraded output side-by-side; note that some names and acronyms get garbled in transcripts but the console stores raw model outputs.
[06:22] Raj: demonstration - i load their 'cardiac triage' prompt set; here's output comparison: fp16 got correct triage 98.6%, int8 96.9% (a few missed red flags), fp8 97.9%. human review notes attached.
[06:46] Priya: 2% drop is scary for triage. what's rollback / monitoring look like?
[07:01] Raj: we provide quality monitors that run prompt sets against live traffic and trigger alerts if accuracy dips vs baseline. you can set automatic rollback to previous profile or route to safe model.
[07:19] Elaine: curious about throughput - our peak concurrency can spike to 400 rps for short bursts. will batching help?
[07:30] Raj: continuous batching helps throughput but increases tail latency if you wait too long; Optimize suggests dynamic batching thresholds based on latency SLOs. also you can provision dedicated pools for guaranteed throughput.
[07:53] Marco: what about canarying across regions? we have data residency constraints in EU.
[08:02] Maya: you can pin rollout by region and by account; private deployments can be restricted to EU zones. we'll include residency notes in the security packet.
[08:20] Raj: switching to the sandbox demo — i've uploaded a small harness that runs 1000 sample prompts and reports latency, token cost, and fidelity deltas. launching run now — estimates 12 min.
[08:37] Elaine: while that runs, quick question about prompts that are long clinical notes (2k tokens) — do you recommend different profiles?
[08:49] Raj: for long contexts int8 sometimes introduces more drift; fp8 or fp16 for long-context is safer. we also suggest prefix caching and KV-sharding for repeated context to keep cost down.
[09:10] [09:10] (brief silence/crosstalk as sandbox starts)
[09:40] Raj: run halfway — early numbers: int8 p50 210ms, fp8 p50 185ms on these longer prompts, but note sample quality: int8 mislabels a medication mention in 3/100.
[10:02] Priya: could we set confidence thresholds to only escalate to human if model confidence low?
[10:10] Raj: yes you can tie a confidence metric and route low confidence to human review or to fp8/backstop model.
[10:25] Maya: just flagging that confidence scoring can be model-dependent; we recommend calibrating during POC.
[10:38] Marco: what about cost models — int8 gives cost wins but risks — do you have a calculator?
[10:45] Lina: yes we have a cost-to-accuracy calculator in Optimize console; i'll share a template spreadsheet.
[10:58] Elaine: are there any known failure modes where fp8 underperforms on medical jargon?
[11:05] Raj: FP8 can sometimes amplify small numerical instabilities in rare tokens, especially with low-frequency vocab. those show up in the heatmap as red cells; we add safety heuristics to detect and route.
[11:23] Jonas: for private on-prem, what's deployment packaging? containerized? helm?
[11:30] Maya: we offer an on-prem package with Kubernetes helm charts and an optional lightweight control plane; infra team provides install runbooks.
[11:47] Elaine: ok, two practical asks: (1) we want the sandbox run output and (2) a short playbook for rollouts and fallback rules.
[11:57] Maya: noted, we'll deliver both.
[12:05] Raj: sandbox finished — summary report link: (shared in chat) — shows p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and the per-prompt fidelity delta.
[12:23] Raj: digging into sample failures - here's an example where int8 turned 'admit for observation' to 'outpatient follow up' on a low-confidence passage; note the human reviewer flagged it as a regression.
[12:42] Elaine: that's exactly the class we were worried about. can we run a sensitivity sweep to find the minimal quantization that preserves those labels?
[12:52] Raj: yes, we can run a sensitivity sweep (int8 per-layer selectively, pct quantization, mixed precision). Optimize console has a guided sweep wizard.
[13:08] Priya: are there any regulatory concerns about storing logs of patient prompts?
[13:16] Maya: absolutely — for PHI we recommend data filtering before sending to hosted, or prefer private deployment with no retention. we can also redact PII client-side.
[13:31] Marco: timeline for a POC - what's realistic? two-week sandbox + four-week pilot?
[13:40] Maya: typical: 2 weeks benchmarking/sensitivity + 4 weeks pilot on dedicated pool. we'll scope a minimal pilot for you.
[13:52] Raj: quick note: some captioning earlier showed 'Redwood Console' as 'Redwood Council' — minor captioning artifact in the transcript generator.
[14:04] Elaine: ok, curious about one more thing - model rollbacks under SLA violations, is that automatic?
[14:15] Raj: you can set automatic rollback on quality or latency thresholds; rollback can be at route-level and will also notify SREs.
[14:29] Priya: can the console export evidence for audits (like sample pairs and timestamps)?
[14:36] Maya: yes, exportable audit bundles with signed timestamps.
[14:48] Jonas: we will want a custom RBAC mapping to restrict devs from changing rollout policies.
[14:56] Maya: supported — RBAC and SSO via SAML/OIDC; we'll include the mapping guide.
[15:10] Marco: one last performance q - if we do dedicated GPU pools, can we pin kernels to force fp8 performance?
[15:19] Raj: yes, dedicated pools can be provisioned with kernel sets optimized for certain precision; our infra will recommend a profile based on your sample workload.
[15:34] Maya: we're almost at time - quick recap: we'll send sandbox outputs, security whitepaper, playbook, and a POC plan. customer to share prompts and SLA targets.
[15:48] Elaine: sounds good, thanks.
[15:53] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the POC kickoff and upload artifacts. bye.

End notes: occasional transcription errors observed ("f p eight" vs "fp8", "K-V cash"). Console links and sandbox artifact were shared in the chat: /shared/sandbox/sunrise-987, /security/Sunrise-SOC2.pdf.
